title: Instagram Modernized Its UI with an AI-Native Architecture, Cutting Token Costs by 33%
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/instagram-compose-migration/en/headerimage/aws-reliability-dns-1792077775251.jpg"/><p>Instagram Direct migrated its Android UI from the legacy Android View system to Jetpack Compose, creating an AI-native UI codebase that is easier for AI coding agents to understand, modify, and maintain. According to Instagram engineers, the migration reduced UI code volume by 50% and token costs per AI agent session by 33%.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Optimizing Software Workflow: Exploring Fundamental Impacts in Technology
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/optimize-software-workflow/en/headerimage/header-1791282094936.jpg"/><p>Software only has value when shipped; faster release cadence matters. Development, deployment, and operations require different thinking, metrics, and investments. There are four impacts in tech: product success, compute capacity, engineering capacity, and strategic innovation. The biggest expense is people. AI shifts engineers toward deeper problem understanding, not fewer engineers.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: What 25 Trillion Tokens Reveal About How Developers Actually Adopt AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/agentic-ai-developer-trust-adoption/en/mediumimage/brendan-oleary-medium-1791452159106.jpeg"/><p>Brendan O'Leary discusses how real-world AI adoption depends on building trust rather than chasing model benchmarks. Drawing from 40 trillion tokens of usage data, he explains the four rungs of the AI adoption ladder and analyzes key failure points in context construction, multi-model routing, and feedback loops to help engineering leaders successfully scale agentic workflows.</p> <i>By Brendan O’Leary</i>

title: Grafana Tempo 3.1 Adds Query-Based Trace Redaction and Sampling-Aware TraceQL Metrics
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/grafana-tempo-31/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791965478500.jpg"/><p>Grafana Labs has released Tempo 3.1, the first minor update to the 3.0 architecture. It adds TLS and additional SASL mechanisms to the Kafka client, lets operators redact traces with a TraceQL query instead of a list of trace IDs, and introduces an experimental query-time hint that corrects TraceQL metrics for sampled data.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Article: Server-Side DPoP and Token Exchange in Spring Security 7
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/spring-security-7-server-side-dpop-token-exchange/en/headerimage/spring-security-7-server-side-dpop-token-exchange-header-1791884636157.jpg"/><p>Spring Authorization Server now lives inside Spring Security 7 under the same Maven coordinates, so the upgrade is a version bump. This server-side guide covers enabling DPoP and RFC 8693 Token Exchange, explains why 7.1 apps can silently stop enforcing DPoP until they call .dPoP(), and shows how to combine both into narrowed, sender-constrained tokens for service-to-service and agentic calls.</p> <i>By Dhruv Agnihotri</i>

title: Meta Extends Confidential Computing to AI Glasses with Private Processing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/meta-private-process-ai-glasses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790823797609.jpg"/><p>Meta has extended Private Processing to AI glasses, using confidential VMs, trusted execution environments, remote attestation, anonymous credentials, OHTTP routing, and TEE-based storage to process AI workloads and persistent user context in the cloud.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: How to Find Resilience Bugs in Systems that Don't Exist
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/formal-methods-principles/en/mediumimage/hillel-wayne-medium-1790846078119.jpeg"/><p>Hillel Wayne discusses how formal methods principles - such as property strength, state-space verification, and environment assumptions - help software engineers uncover critical architectural bugs early. He shares practical mental models like "adversarial non-determinism" to reason about concurrency, edge cases, and distributed system failures without needing complex mathematical tools.</p> <i>By Hillel Wayne</i>

title: Article: Composable Commerce: Inside Shipt’s Kit Platform
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/shipt-composable-commerce-design-ddd/en/headerimage/shipt-composable-commerce-design-ddd-header-1791812515573.jpg"/><p>Shipt launched its Kits feature, enabling quick assembly of themed grocery bundles for events. The platform architecture lets merchandisers easily create store-aware kits, streamlining previously labor-intensive workflows. It utilizes a flexible model of items, shopping lists, and kits to ensure kits display accurately based on local inventory and customer needs.</p> <i>By Khurshid Hameed</i>

title: Google Antigravity SDK Adds Local Model Support for Greater Token Efficiency and Code Privacy
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/antigravity-sdk-local-models/en/headerimage/agent-friendly-android-cli-1791967537412.jpeg"/><p>Google has introduced support for local models in the Antigravity SDK, enabling developers to build and execute agentic workflows directly on their own machines, while retaining the flexibility to mix in cloud-based models for higher-level tasks. This approach gives developers greater control over data privacy, inference costs, network dependencies, and computational workload distribution.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Cloudflares Newly Acquired Vite+ Reaches 1.0 with GitLab CI Support, Hooks, and tsup Migration
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-viteplus-stable/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791892196672.jpg"/><p>VoidZero has launched Vite+ 1.0, the first stable version of its JavaScript toolchain. It features a command line tool for managing Node.js, package management, and frontend development from a single configuration file. Enhancements include CI integration for GitLab and Docker support. Future updates are planned, focusing on stability and diagnostics.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/backstage-1-55-task-recovery/en/headerimage/header-1791490255579.jpeg"/><p>Backstage 1.55 adds opt-in recovery for Software Template tasks, resuming crashed or timed-out runs from the last completed step. The release also carries breaking changes to the catalog, search and TechDocs, so teams should review their configuration before upgrading to the current 1.55.3 patch.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: ZCS Command Injection via SNMP Handlers Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/zimbra-command-injection/en/headerimage/headerZimbra-1791879318550.jpg"/><p>A critical remote command execution vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite, identified as CVE-2026-73570, poses risks by allowing unauthorized access to mailbox data and credentials. This flaw, stemming from improper input sanitization, has been actively exploited. Organizations are advised to upgrade to version 10.1.20 or disable susceptible SNMP services to mitigate risks.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Production Patterns for Agents, Evals, and LLM Costs: QCon AI New York 2026
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-sessionsv2/en/headerimage/qcon-ai-new-york-2026-1791875885339.jpg"/><p>Once AI is in production, code arrives faster than it can be reviewed, token costs rise, evals have to be good enough to act on, and agents need permissions and guardrails. QCon AI New York 2026 (December 15-16) has confirmed sessions from engineers sharing how they handle these constraints.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-eventbridge-scaling/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791474735792.jpg"/><p>AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: How Eve Online Leverages Head Based Sampling to Observe "Fun"
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/eve-observability-head-sampling/en/mediumimage/nicholas-herring-medium-1791444748399.jpg"/><p>Nicholas Herring shares how EVE Online tackles distributed tracing and observability across a 20-year-old MMO architecture. He discusses leveraging head-based, dynamic exponential moving average (EMA), and deterministic sampling techniques to maintain high system fidelity, control telemetry costs, and avoid performance degradation under high-throughput real-time game simulations.</p> <i>By Nicholas Herring</i>
